sources: Sun Aug 16 weekend run, capturing Friday Aug 14 closes. THEME: the household sector broke on Friday while the volatility complex kept melting - the widest divergence between hard data and market pricing so far this cycle. THE STORY IS UMICH: August preliminary consumer sentiment 51.0 (U. Michigan, released Aug 14 10am ET), DOWN 7.6% from 55.2 July final and a huge miss vs 54.5 consensus - ends two months of recovery, current conditions -5.5% to 51.8, expectations -8.7% to 50.6, year-ahead inflation expectations UP to 4.3% from 4.2%, expected business conditions -11% short run and -17% long run, and only 8% of consumers expect income to outpace inflation. Declines were broad across the political spectrum, sharpest among older, lower-income and non-college households. It landed alongside July retail sales -0.6% m/m vs +0.1% expected. Two consecutive soft consumer datapoints now sit next to last week's broken sub-200k claims streak. Brent 88.52 Aug 14 (TradingEconomics), UP 1.67% on the day and more than 5% on the week as the US escalated pressure on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz - the risk premium is back and now overrides the IEA/OPEC demand downgrades that capped crude last week. VIX 14.25 Aug 14 close, DOWN 2.6% from 14.63 and the LOWEST CLOSE OF 2026 - equity vol is pricing sub-1% daily S&P moves on the same day the consumer cracked. MOVE ~69.6 Aug 14 (Barchart $MOVE, cross-checked vs Yahoo ^MOVE 69.23 Aug 13; +/-0.4), DOWN from 72.0 and from 83.0 on Aug 3 - bond vol at the dormant end of its post-2021 range. Both vol gauges at cycle lows into deteriorating hard data is the setup that historically precedes repricing, not the setup that follows it. 10Y-2Y +0.51 Aug 14 (FRED T10Y2Y; 10Y 4.68 minus 2Y 4.17), UP from 0.48 Aug 12 - bear-steepening continues, front end rallying on cut pricing. T5YIFR 2.30% Aug 14 (FRED via Convex), essentially unchanged vs 2.28 in the last file but DOWN 1.3% over 7 days - breakevens are not confirming the crude move, consistent with a demand-side read on the consumer data. HY OAS 271bp Aug 13 (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2; Aug 14 not yet published), flat w/w (+0.37% 1W) and pinned in the richest decile, ~180bp inside the long-run median. Credit has not blinked at UMich - watch this for the first crack. BDTI 2742 Aug 14 (derived from StockQ YTD +107.88% and Barchart BDTI.BI base 1319; +/-15pts), UP ~2% on the day and ~+50 w/w - Baltic Exchange Week 33 report describes a generally positive dirty market, Suezmax TCE UP >30k/day to 269,824 on Atlantic Basin tightness while VLCC eased to 234,821 from 241,916. Freight remains the deepest red reading on the board. EUR/USD 3M xccy -10bp CARRIED - no free dated quote; secondary estimates cluster -15 to -20bp, no stress event in the window, carried rather than moved to avoid a false threshold trip. NFCI -0.55 CARRIED (Chicago Fed, week ending Aug 7, next release Aug 19). Global liquidity 1=stable. DXY 99.80 Aug 14 (TradingEconomics/FXStreet), a one-week low after retail sales and UMich; opened near 100.00 before piercing 99.50 - flat vs 99.57 a week ago, the dollar is not trading the data. Copper 6.59/lb and Gold 4387.62/oz Aug 14 close (TradingEconomics) -> ratio 1.50, flat vs 1.49; gold topped 4,400 intraday on cooling CPI and Fed-hold repricing while copper drifted, a mildly negative growth mix. Claims 209k CARRIED (wk Aug 8, next release Aug 20 - the print that shows whether the broken sub-200k streak was noise). ISM Manufacturing 55.6 July CARRIED, August prints Sep 1. SOFR-OIS ~2bp CARRIED, SOFR itself 3.62% Aug 13 (NY Fed), no funding stress. LEI -1.4% YoY June CARRIED, July release Aug 20. Sahm Rule -0.03 July CARRIED, no labour-recession trigger. Permits 1367k June CARRIED, July release Aug 18. WATCH THIS WEEK: building permits Aug 18, NFCI Aug 19, jobless claims and LEI Aug 20.
